title: udev: regression?
body:
#26886 may cause a regression. I am not sure. This is just a reminder.

https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/26886#issuecomment-1636666910
> This seems to have caused a regression, see https://bugs.debian.org/cgi-bin/bugreport.cgi?bug=1040956
> 
> @participant1 can you please take a look?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: @participant2 Could you provide which rule causes the issue?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Also, please provide the results of `udevadm info DEVICE` and `udevadm test DEVICE`.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Debian bug submitter here. I would guess the offending udev rule will be in https://salsa.debian.org/Mobian-team/devices/librem5-tweaks/-/blob/mobian/debian/mobian-librem5-tweaks.librem5-pm.udev.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Hmm, I cannot find anything suspicious in the udev rules file or any other in the package.

This has nothing to do with `power/persist`. The rules affected by systemd change that aren't being set anymore (which in turn causes USB resets) are:

These have been already changed upstream to a version that still works with newer systemd:
```
SUBSYSTEM=="usb", ENV{DEVPATH}=="/devices/platform/soc@0/38200000.usb/xhci-hcd.4.auto/usb1/1-0:1.0", ATTR{usb1-port1/quirks}="10000000"

Nope, that's not what `power/persist` does ;) It applies when the power session is broken, and merely suspending a device does not break its power session.
